Plot Predicted Mortality Over Time by Treatment Arm

plot_mortality_curves.Rd

Extracts patient death times from WARDEN DES simulation output, fits a Kaplan-Meier survival curve per treatment arm pooled across all PSA samples, and returns a ggplot step plot of predicted overall survival.

Usage

plot_mortality_curves(
  runresults,
  n_samples,
  n_patients,
  n_treatments,
  trt_names
)

Arguments

runresults

List of length n_samples. Each element is a WARDEN simulation result containing a merged_df data frame with columns pat_id, arm, evtname, and evttime.

n_samples

Integer. Number of PSA samples run.

n_patients

Integer. Number of simulated patients per sample.

n_treatments

Integer. Number of treatment arms.

trt_names

Character vector of length n_treatments giving treatment arm names. Must match values in merged_df$arm.

Value

A ggplot object. The plot shows survival probability (y-axis, 0 to 1) against time in years (x-axis, 0 to 65), with one step line per treatment arm distinguished by colour and linetype. The legend is positioned at the bottom.

Details

Death times are extracted by filtering merged_df to rows where evtname == "death" for each combination of sample, treatment arm, and patient. Times are stored in a three-dimensional array [n_samples x n_treatments x n_patients] and sorted within each [sample, treatment] slice before KM fitting.

KM curves are fitted using survfit with all patients pooled across PSA samples for each treatment arm, treating every patient as experiencing the event (no censoring). Linetype cycles through "solid", "dashed", "dotted", "dotdash" if there are more than four treatment arms.

See also

rrmsdesmodel, survfit

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
msdes::rrmsdessetup(drc = 0.035, drq = 0.035, time_horizon = 70,
                    p_eid = 0, jcvtest_cost = 0)
msdes::rrmsdesmodel(n_patients = 10, n_samples = 100)

msdes::plot_mortality_curves(
  runresults   = results[[1]],
  n_samples    = 100,
  n_patients   = 10,
  n_treatments = n_treatments,
  trt_names    = v_treatment_names
)
} # }
